§28.11 Expansions in Series of Mathieu Functions

ⓘ
Keywords:
Mathieu functions, expansions in series of
Notes:
See Arscott (1964b, §3.9.1).
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/28.11
See also:
Annotations for Ch.28

Let f⁡(z) be a 2⁢π-periodic function that is analytic in an open doubly-infinite strip S that contains the real axis, and q be a normal value (§28.7). Then

28.11.1 f⁡(z)=α0⁢ce0⁡(z,q)+∑n=1∞(αn⁢cen⁡(z,q)+βn⁢sen⁡(z,q)),
ⓘ
Defines:
f⁡(z): function (locally)
Symbols:
cen⁡(z,q): Mathieu function, sen⁡(z,q): Mathieu function, q=h2: parameter, n: integer, z: complex variable, αn and βn
Referenced by:
§28.11

http://dlmf.nist.gov/28.11.E1
Encodings:

See also:

where

28.11.2 αn =1π⁢∫02⁢πf⁡(x)⁢cen⁡(x,q)⁢dx,
βn =1π⁢∫02⁢πf⁡(x)⁢sen⁡(x,q)⁢dx.
ⓘ
Defines:
αn (locally) and βn (locally)
Symbols:
cen⁡(z,q): Mathieu function, sen⁡(z,q): Mathieu function, π: the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, dx: differential of x, ∫: integral, q=h2: parameter, n: integer, x: real variable and f⁡(z): function
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/28.11.E2
Encodings:
TeX, TeX, pMML, pMML, png, png
See also:
Annotations for §28.11 and Ch.28

The series (28.11.1) converges absolutely and uniformly on any compact subset of the strip S. See Meixner and Schäfke (1954, §2.28), and for expansions in the case of the exceptional values of q see Meixner et al. (1980, p. 33).
